This study proposes an anomalous sound detection system that learns from normal recordings without external pre-training and uses machine-type information to organize training and normal references. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.18103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An Acoustic Room Transformation (ART) method is proposed for clinical applications to render simulated acoustic environments using six loudspeakers in a reverberant room. In typical clinical settings, testing rooms are not acoustically treated and only a limited number of loudspeakers are available. The ART approach enables control of the playback-room reverberation, allowing speech intelligibility tests to be performed under realistic and perceptually compensated conditions. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.18330v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech applications require decisions about term presence, turn completion, and language within an audio window. We present Marimba, an interface for typed speech decisions built on frozen Qwen3-ASR 0.6B features. Lexical questions use zero-shot scoring of ASR transcripts; non-lexical questions use a question-conditioned head and a separate layer-18 turn-end readout. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.17599v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) have been interpreted either as cochlear standing waves or as local oscillations of hair cells. Multiple SOAE lines test both views, because each view must explain how the lines coexist. In the standing-wave view, each line is a separate resonance. In the intermodulation view, some lines are distortion products of others. Both explanations assume several independent oscillations. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Cross-Linguistic Acoustic Biomarkers of Cognitive Impairment Across Interactive and Single-Speaker Speech Tasks
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.17710v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Multilingual dementia detection is essential for scalable and equitable screening. In recent years, automated speech analysis has emerged as a promising approach for supporting dementia detection by enabling non-invasive and scalable assessment of cognitive function. However, existing studies that use automated speech analysis often rely on one type of task, such as picture description, and use black-box models. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.18050v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: When a conversational Voice AI agent places an outbound call, the far end may be a live person, a voicemail greeting, an interactive voice response (IVR) system, or increasingly another AI system answering on the callee's behalf. Standard Answering Machine Detection (AMD) reports only whether a human or a machine picked up, a design meant for human call centres, where one machine is as uninteresting as another. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.35581v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: When a user talks over a full-duplex dialogue model, it must decide whether the user is interrupting (stop) or backchannelling (carry on). Post-training can improve this discrimination or change how readily it stops. In our GRPO runs the second dominates: no configuration lowers both error rates on more than one model, and two released checkpoints discriminate no better than their bases. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2603.16411v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Entity recognition in Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) is challenging for rare and domain-specific terms. In domains such as finance, medicine, and air-traffic control, these errors are costly. If an entity is entirely absent from the ASR output, text-only post-correction has little signal to recover it. To address this, we introduce RECOVER, an agentic post-ASR entity-correction framework. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: GigaEdge Spench: An SDK for Practical Streaming Speech Enhancement
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.13243v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We present GigaEdge Spench, an open-source SDK for streaming speech enhancement on CPU servers, mobile devices, and in browsers. Applications can build enhancement channels from neural denoising, normalization and dynamics blocks, sample-rate conversion, and acoustic echo cancellation where supported. These stages can be combined, while normalization can also run without a neural model. The release includes an 8 kHz INT8 denoiser and discriminative and hybrid 48 kHz FP32 models. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: CoTTAGE: An Explainable Judge for Text-to-Audio Generation
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.17644v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rapid progress in text-to-audio (TTA) generation demands reliable and explainable automatic evaluation. However, existing metrics fail to simultaneously deliver high correlation with human judgments and meaningful, audio-grounded explanations, forcing reliance on labor-intensive human evaluation that bottlenecks model development iteration. To address this, we propose CoTTAGE, a reasoning-based evaluator for text relevance (REL) and audio quality (OVL). Following a reason-then-predict paradigm, CoTTAGE first generates an audio-grounded rationale

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Any Channel Count, One Token Stream: Incorporating Spatial Audio Understanding and Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.18112v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio phase relations encode source locations, yet existing large audio-language models (LALM) reduce audio to single-channel content to stabilise general audio understanding, leaving spatial information for direction, distance, and source-relation questions unused. We present SpheraAudio, which accepts recordings with any channel count -- mono, stereo, First-Order Ambisonics (FOA), or higher -- and maps them into a single token stream. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: eDIAR: Training-Free Open-Speaker Streaming Diarization for Long Meetings and Large Archives via e-means
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.18529v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Meetings last up to an hour, and nobody knows in advance how many people will speak. Neural diarizers with a fixed number of output slots, such as Streaming Sortformer and Nemotron-3, are accurate and run online, but they cannot name more speakers than they have slots. We remove this limit without retraining. The slot head keeps deciding who is active and when speech overlaps, and speaker embeddings are clustered inside a single slot, with the official e-means algorithm, only after every slot has been used. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: CamSpokenNLI: A Pilot Resource for Cross-Variety Transfer Evaluation in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.17573v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Cameroon Pidgin English (a West African Pidgin English variety) and Camfranglais are widely used in Cameroon, yet to our knowledge, neither has a dedicated spoken Natural Language Inference (NLI) resource. We introduce CamSpokenNLI, a pilot dataset of 114 scenario-matched spoken NLI items in each variety (228 in total), recorded by one native speaker from Buea. The novella is a study of what happens when the scale of a phenomenon exceeds the practical and conceptual frameworks available to comprehend it and of the paralysis that sometimes follows a demand for action in such overwhelming circumstances. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: ZONOS3-Mini Technical Report
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.16525v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: ZONOS3-Mini is an ultra-compact, ultra-fast, zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model. The model can run in real time on a laptop or smartphone. For its latency and size, it achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and cloning fidelity. To achieve this we propose a latent MoE backbone with only 886M parameters (100M active per token) and a new audio codec, Zyphra Audio Codec 1 (ZAC-1), which represents 44.1 kHz audio at a 15 Hz frame rate.
